title: Biodiversity and Ecosystems
text: Biodiversity refers to the variety of life on Earth at all levels, from genes to ecosystems. Earth is estimated to have 8.7 million species of eukaryotes, of which only about 1.2 million have been described and cataloged. Biodiversity is crucial for ecosystem functioning: diverse ecosystems are more resilient to disturbances and provide ecosystem services including food, clean water, pollination, and climate regulation. The Amazon rainforest, despite covering only about 5.5 million km² (less than 4% of Earth's land surface), harbors about 10% of all species on Earth. Current extinction rates are estimated to be 100–1,000 times higher than natural background rates, leading scientists to call this era the Sixth Mass Extinction.
